proposal.description: sync_out is made a sticky latch: once a 1 has passed through it holds 1 until rst_n, as if every synchronised input were a latched fault flag
proposal.reason: With RESET_VALUE=0, after async_in goes high and then low, sync_out stays 1 instead of following it back to 0 two clocks later. With RESET_VALUE=1, sync_out never leaves 1 after reset.

proposal.description: A 'fast fault path': the safe/asserted level (RESET_VALUE) goes from async_in straight to sync_out, and only the release goes through meta_ff
proposal.reason: When async_in moves to RESET_VALUE, sync_out shows it one clock later instead of two, and a one-clock pulse to RESET_VALUE that meta_ff never samples still reaches sync_out. Moves away from RESET_VALUE still take two clocks.

proposal.description: RESET_VALUE is read as an input-polarity setting, so the first stage stores async_in inverted whenever RESET_VALUE is 1
proposal.reason: In instances with RESET_VALUE=1 (CS_n, CP, OTP, UVLO, latch_stat), sync_out after reset is the inverse of async_in, two clocks later. With RESET_VALUE=0 nothing changes.

proposal.description: During reset sync_out shifts in meta_ff instead of being forced to RESET_VALUE, so a stale first-stage sample survives reset entry and power-up leaves sync_out undefined until a clock edge
proposal.reason: When rst_n falls, sync_out takes the old meta_ff value, not RESET_VALUE, and keeps it until the next clk edge. At power-up with no clock yet, sync_out stays X/undefined instead of RESET_VALUE.
